items.title: SC asks HDFC, ICICI bank to grant prosecution sanction in subvention fraud
items.rss_summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of their officials within a week in alleged subvention scheme frauds involving real estate developers, banks and financial institutions. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these financial institutions would have to personally appear before it in case of non-compliance. "We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them," the bench said in its order. Under the subvention scheme, banks disburse the sanctioned amount directly to the accounts of builders, who are then required to pay the EMIs until the flats are handed over to homebuyers. items.hinglish_title: Subvention Fraud: Supreme Court Ka HDFC Aur ICICI Ko Ek Hafte Ka Ultimetam

CJI Surya Kant ki bench ne chetavni di ki non-compliance par bank ke CMD aur Chairman ko court mein hazir hona hoga. Subvention scheme mein banks seedha builders ko amount bhejte the jinhe homebuyer ke possession lene tak EMI bharni thi, jisme alleged fraud hua hai.

items.title: HC to hear Tata Trusts' plea against Chandra's reappointment on Friday
items.rss_summary: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) on Thursday filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term. The court will hear the matter on Friday. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has sought Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest. As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA). Senior counsel Janak Dwarkadas, appearing for the two trusts, mentioned the suits on Thursday before a single bench of Justice Arif Doctor, seeking an urgent hearing. Justice Doctor, however, recused himself without assigning any reasons, following which the suits were mentioned before Justice Abhay Ahuja, who was sitting on the alternate bench. Dwar

Trusts ne daawa kiya hai ki September 17 ka Tata Sons ka board resolution Articles of Association ke Article 121 ke mutabiq invalid hai. SDTT ne ₹50 crore aur RDTT ne ₹15 crore ke damages ki maang ki hai, jiski sunwayi Friday ko hogi.

items.title: Sebi appoints auditor to probe Coffee Day Enterprises' fund diversion
items.rss_summary: Markets regulator SEBI has appointed a forensic auditor to assist in a probe into the affairs of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd, following directions from the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT). The SAT had on November 5 directed the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to conduct a fresh, independent and comprehensive investigation into the alleged diversion of Rs 3,535 crore from seven subsidiaries of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd (CDEL) to Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estates Ltd (MACEL), an entity linked to the company's promoters. Pursuant to the order dated November 5, 2026 passed by the appellate tribunal, CDEL, in a regulatory filing on Thursday, said "SEBI has, vide its letter dated November 25, 2026, informed the company that CLA Indus Value Consulting has been appointed as the forensic auditor to assist the investigating authority." The company said its board of directors would take further steps as may be necessary in the matter. On November 5, SAT set aside an order ..

Regulatory filing mein company ne bataya ki CLA Indus Value Consulting ko investigating authority ki madad ke liye appoint kiya gaya hai.
